title: Information Ecology Mechanisms — Repetition, Correction, Context, Reward and Digital Memory
purpose: Ground the Information Ecology & Memory Room in named empirical and conceptual mechanisms rather than generic claims about virality, memory and platforms.
epistemic_rule: These studies describe population-level tendencies, experiments, reviews and legal frameworks. They do not establish that any particular person believed a claim because of repetition, that any platform intentionally caused a specific outcome, or that one mechanism explains every online conflict.

mechanisms.name: Illusory truth effect
mechanisms.finding: Repeated statements tend to receive higher truth ratings than novel statements. A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of 182 studies / 366 effect sizes / 31,184 participants reported a small but robust bias-corrected effect (g = 0.37, 95% CI 0.30–0.44), with substantial heterogeneity.
mechanisms.moderators: The meta-analysis found that initial task, presentation duration and explicit veracity cues helped explain heterogeneity. Requiring a truth judgment during initial exposure substantially reduced the later repetition effect relative to passive or irrelevant processing.
mechanisms.project_use: Track exposure count separately from source independence and factual status. Repetition is evidence about familiarity and diffusion, not corroboration.

mechanisms.name: Repetition can increase belief in misinformation
mechanisms.finding: A 2024 review reports that repetition can increase belief in fake-news headlines, conspiracy claims and even some claims that conflict with prior knowledge; effects can extend beyond belief to sharing intentions and moral judgments.
mechanisms.boundary: The effect is robust but not universal. Content, task, plausibility, prior knowledge and accuracy attention matter.

mechanisms.name: Corrections usually improve accuracy, but memory is not perfectly rewritten
mechanisms.finding: A 2024 review concludes that factual corrections generally improve belief accuracy across many countries, political beliefs and demographic groups, while classic 'backfire' effects are exceedingly rare. Separate memory research shows that corrected misinformation can continue influencing inference and that correction effects weaken over time when the correction or its source is forgotten.
mechanisms.project_use: Do not encode the folk rule 'corrections make misinformation stronger'. Instead record correction, current status, correction visibility, source credibility and later recurrence separately.

mechanisms.name: Correction design matters
mechanisms.finding: A 2023 review recommends detailed corrections, alternative explanations, reminders of the initial misinformation and repetition of the correction. It reports limited evidence that merely restating misinformation inside a correction commonly causes harmful backfire.
mechanisms.project_use: A correction record should explain what changed and what replaces the old account, not merely stamp a red label on the old claim.

mechanisms.name: Repetition and source independence are different variables
mechanisms.finding: Research on eyewitness misinformation found that repetition, rather than simply the number of apparent sources, can increase susceptibility and confidence. More broadly, a copied claim can create many visible artifacts without creating many independent observations.
mechanisms.project_use: Represent source lineage. Ten screenshots descending from one post are ten distribution events but may still represent one root evidentiary source.

mechanisms.name: Context collapse
mechanisms.finding: Context collapse describes online communication in which different audiences, expectations and background assumptions overlap around the same post. Recent work emphasizes that this can be understood as multiple overlapping language games rather than a single homogeneous audience.
mechanisms.counterpoint: Ethnographic research also shows that users can actively reconstruct audience boundaries through privacy settings, multiple accounts and platform practices; context collapse is an affordance/problem tendency, not an inevitable state.
mechanisms.project_use: Archive the intended audience, original thread/room, surrounding turns and later receiving audience when interpretation depends on context.

mechanisms.name: Social feedback can alter posting behavior
mechanisms.finding: A 2021 Nature Communications study modeled 1,046,857 posts from 4,168 users across four datasets and found patterns consistent with reward learning. An online experiment also found that manipulated social-reward rates causally changed posting latency.
mechanisms.boundary: This supports a reward-learning contribution to social-media behavior; it does not show that every user is addicted or that likes explain all posting behavior.
mechanisms.project_use: Treat likes/replies/notifications as possible behavioral feedback variables, not as simple measures of truth, agreement or well-being.

mechanisms.name: Platformized collective memory
mechanisms.finding: A 2025 review describes social media as reshaping collective remembering and forgetting through algorithmic curation, hashtag commemoration, memetic memory and digital memory activism, while identifying data-access limits, Western-centric bias and AI as an emerging memory agent.
mechanisms.project_use: Collective memory should be modeled as an active retrieval/circulation process, not merely a static archive of old objects.

mechanisms.name: Preservation, search prominence and erasure are legally distinct
mechanisms.finding: EU data-protection law provides a right to erasure in defined circumstances, but the right is not absolute and can yield to freedom of expression, legal obligations, public-interest archiving and legal claims. Name-based search delisting can also differ from deletion of the underlying publication.
mechanisms.project_use: Historical preservation and present discoverability should be represented as separate states. A true old record can remain historically important while becoming misleading if surfaced without date or current-status context.

room_tests: Exposure count must never be displayed as independent-source count.
Corrections should be linked from the original and the original should expose its current correction/status.
Sensitive identity labels need event date, publication date, current status and last review where possible.
Portable fragments should retain a route back to a context envelope: speaker, audience, thread, date, surrounding turns and source.
Platform metrics are behavioral traces. They are not direct truth, consensus, intent or value measurements.
When an archive makes a present-tense statement from an old record, verify that the state is still current.
When a claim is highly repeated, require an explicit accuracy/provenance check rather than granting it evidentiary weight from familiarity.
